# Draft:Council of Scientific Society Presidents

----
The Council of Scientific Society Presidents (CSSP) is a United States–based nonprofit organization founded in 1973 that brings together the elected leadership of major scientific and engineering societies. It serves as a forum for discussion of science policy, leadership, and issues affecting the scientific enterprise in the United States.
History
CSSP was established in 1973 during a period of expansion in federal investment in scientific research and increasing attention to national science policy.
Historical analyses of U.S. science policy describe the late 20th century as a period in which scientific societies became more coordinated in their interactions with government and public policy institutions. Organizations such as CSSP emerged within this broader context as mechanisms for communication among scientific leadership across disciplines.
Contemporary reporting described CSSP as a venue for scientific society leaders to address cross-disciplinary issues including research funding, education, and the role of science in public policy.
Organization
CSSP is composed of the leadership of member scientific and engineering societies, typically including presidents, presidents-elect, and immediate past presidents.
The organization does not conduct research or administer grants. Instead, it functions as a coordinating body facilitating communication across disciplines and institutions.
Archival correspondence from U.S. science policy officials has described CSSP as representing multiple scientific societies and as a potential source of expertise for federal science and technology leadership.
Activities
Policy discussions
CSSP convenes meetings and discussions focused on science policy, federal research funding, and emerging scientific issues. These meetings have included participation from federal agencies, academic institutions, and scientific societies.
Studies of scientific societies describe such forums as mechanisms for coordinating perspectives across disciplines and improving engagement with public policy.
Role in scientific coordination
Research on the structure of science in the United States has identified professional societies as key intermediaries between researchers, institutions, and policymakers.
Broader studies of scientific communities describe how networks and umbrella groups of scientific societies can facilitate coordination across disciplines and contribute to shared policy perspectives.
Analyses of U.S. science institutions further note that collective organization among scientific societies can shape how research priorities are articulated to policymakers and the public.
Awards
CSSP administers the Carl Sagan Award for Public Understanding of Science, established in 1993 to recognize contributions to public appreciation of science.
Role in the science policy landscape
Analyses of the U.S. science policy system describe a network of institutions that includes federal agencies, advisory bodies, and professional societies.
Within this system, organizations composed of scientific society leadership have been described as facilitating communication and coordination rather than serving as formal advisory bodies.
CSSP has been characterized within this broader landscape as a forum for interaction among scientific leaders across disciplines.
Influence
CSSP's influence is generally characterized as indirect. By bringing together leaders of major scientific societies, it provides a venue for cross-disciplinary discussion and the development of shared perspectives on issues such as research funding, science education, and public engagement.
Research on science policy institutions suggests that coordination among scientific societies can influence how scientific priorities are communicated in broader policy discussions.
